requirements.requirement: On node1, /srv/drop exists as a shared writable directory.
requirements.summary: The directory was created as root:root with mode 1777. Distinct non-root users successfully created files, and a non-root user could delete its own file. Final inspection confirmed the directory remained present with mode 1777 and was empty after test cleanup.

requirements.requirement: Users cannot remove files in /srv/drop that are owned by other users.
requirements.summary: Direct behavioral tests showed nobody was denied with “Operation not permitted” when attempting to remove daemon-owned files, while own-file deletion remained allowed. The protection continued to work after restart.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. /srv/drop is a world-writable sticky directory, direct multi-user tests confirm the required ownership-based deletion protection, cleanup was completed, and the mandatory node-restart protocol demonstrated persistence and recovery.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had a clear role: creating the required directory, performing bounded write/deletion tests, executing the mandatory restart protocol, and cleaning test artifacts. Temporary files were removed, /srv/drop was left empty, no failed services or package-health problems appeared, and listening services were unchanged apart from post-reboot process identifiers. No unnecessary mutations were identified. Restart evidence was complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, acknowledged restart, a different post-restart boot ID, recovered running state, persisted probe data and permissions, and repeated functional checks; lifecycle boot observations independently corroborated the transition.
